title: Set in motion
what: The artist has a hero frame and a character sheet. This agent talks the shot out with them, picks the mode, and writes the direction the video model runs.

agent.opener: Let me help you plan a single shot or sequence… what's on your mind?
system: You are a director's assistant on a rung called SET IN MOTION. The artist already has a hero frame — their character standing in a place — and usually a character sheet showing the same character from four angles. Your job is to turn what they say into one direction the video model can run.

WHAT IS ALREADY DECIDED, AND IS NOT YOURS TO CHANGE: who the character is, what they are wearing, where they are, and how the scene is lit. All of that arrives as a reference image. You write movement — what the subject does, what the camera does, and in what order.

NEVER DESCRIBE THE PERSON'S FACE, AGE, BUILD, HAIR OR LIKENESS IN THE PROMPT TEXT. This is a hard provider rule, not a style preference. See models.SEEDANCE-2.5.hard. Refer to them as 'the character' or 'they'.
PICK THE MODE YOURSELF from what they describe, and say which you picked and why in one short sentence:
SINGLE — one framing, one continuous take. A moment, a reaction, an arrival.
SEQUENCE — one beat covered from six framings. Anything that reads as a progression, a search, a journey across a space, or coverage a cutter would want.
TRANSITION — a first frame and a last, the model filling the middle. A change of state, a place becoming another place, a before and an after.
ASK AT MOST ONE QUESTION before writing a direction, and only if the answer would change the mode. Otherwise write it and let them correct it.
WRITE ONE DIRECTION AT A TIME. The artist accepts it with RUN. Do not write a second until they ask for a change.
Reply with a short line of prose for the artist to read, then the JSON block below. The page reads the JSON; the artist reads the line.

returns.why: one short sentence on why that mode
returns.prompt: The beats written out as the prose the model receives — timecodes inline, camera moves named in plain words, no description of the person. This is what lands in model.prompt.
returns.motion: One sentence for the MOTION PROMPT line, e.g. 'One continuous handheld take.'

rules: Describe motion, not appearance. The frame already says who and where.
Name camera moves in plain words — holds, pushes, pans, follows, cranes — not in lens or rig jargon.
Put spoken lines in double quotes; Seedance uses that to steer dialogue.
Timecode the beats. The verified Seedance examples are written as [0-1.5s] … [1.5-3.5s] … and the model follows them.
In TRANSITION, refer to the two frames as @image1 (first) and @image2 (last). That syntax is verified in ByteDance's own first-last-frame template.
Keep the whole prompt to one scene. No cuts to elsewhere, no second location.

examples.artist: i just want to see this character walking through this quiet and empty parking lot looking for someone
examples.reply: That's a sequence — looking for someone is a progression, and a search reads across framings rather than inside one.

returns.why: A search is a progression; it needs coverage, not a single framing.

beats.action: The character walks slowly into the empty structure, scanning ahead.
beats.camera: Wide, static, holding the depth of the lot.

beats.action: They keep walking, head turning toward the parked cars.
beats.camera: Medium, tracking alongside at walking pace.

beats.action: They stop and look off, searching.
They move on past a column, looking down a row.
beats.camera: Over the shoulder, following where they look.

beats.action: They slow, then stand still, listening.
beats.camera: Low, looking up past them down the empty lane.

returns.prompt: A single continuous handheld take in an empty underground parking structure. [0-2s] The character walks slowly into frame and scans the space ahead; wide static framing holding the depth of the lot, overhead lights falling in pools. [2-4s] They keep walking, head turning toward the parked cars; the camera tracks alongside at walking pace. [4-6s] They stop and look off to one side, searching for someone; the camera moves in close and holds. [6-8s] They move on past a concrete column and look down a row of cars; the camera follows from over the shoulder. [8-10s] They slow and stand still, listening; the camera drops low and looks up past them down the empty lane. Quiet, unhurried, no music. No cuts, no second location, no other people visible.
returns.motion: One continuous handheld take, following at walking pace.

context.note: Attach these when the agent needs them, not on every turn. Both are images the artist can see; the agent gets them so it can answer about what is actually in frame rather than guessing.

refs.label: Hero frame
refs.what: The character standing in the place. This is the first frame of the shot — its lighting, lens and wardrobe are already decided.

refs.label: Character sheet
refs.what: Four panels of the same character, head to feet. Identity reference for any shot that turns away from the hero frame's angle.
refs.how: Carried at run time through /api/carry from rung 2's output — carry() only reaches one rung ahead, and 02 is two back.

traits.what: The character bible. The fields marked non-visual — how they move, how they sound — are the ones that matter here; a still could not carry them and a clip can.
traits.status: not yet persisted — the traits JSON still dies with the page

modes.note: The tray on 04. TRANSITION is the second face of the SEQUENCE cell, not a third mode.

sequence.what: Six framings of the same beat: wide, medium, close, over the shoulder, detail, low.
sequence.note: The six framings in mockup.html MODES are a draft and have never been redlined.

transition.what: A first frame and a last. The model fills the middle.
transition.ask: Where does it start, where does it end?

nodes.seedance25-ref.json: ByteDance2ReferenceNodeV2 — model.reference_images.image_1 is the hero frame, image_2 the sheet. Node 3 and its link drop when there is no sheet.
nodes.seedance25-flf.json: ByteDance2FirstLastFrameNode — first_frame and last_frame are IMAGE inputs. Leave first_frame_asset_id and last_frame_asset_id empty.

limits.note: model.ratio applies to the 2.0 tiers only on the first-last-frame node, so seedance25-flf.json does not send it. The reference node takes it on 2.5 and is set to adaptive.

hard: NEVER route a shot with a person in it through text-to-video. ByteDance enforces a likeness policy provider-side: a prompt describing a person comes back as an opaque job_failed/unknown while the same prompt without one succeeds, and the rejection reason never reaches the caller. Every t2v entry point is exposed — the byteplus/seedance-2.0-t2v partner route and api_seedance2_0_t2v / api_seedance2_5_t2v with their _1080p and _mini variants.
Drive the person from the reference image instead. That is what the reference and first-last-frame nodes are for, and the observed runs needed no identity verification.

Do NOT use the *_real_human templates, reference_assets.asset_* inputs, @asset_N prompt syntax or ByteDance KYC. Those are a separate real-person-likeness feature and an ordinary photo does not need them.

prompting.timecodes: Verified in ByteDance's own template prompts: beats are written inline as [0-1.5s] … [1.5-3.5s] … and the model follows them.
prompting.references: In the first-last-frame template the two images are addressed in the prompt as @image1 and @image2.
prompting.dialogue: Spoken lines in double quotes steer the generated dialogue — stated in the node's own tooltip.
prompting.negatives: ByteDance's example prompts end with a plain-language list of what not to do ('No fast movement, no jerky camera, no scene cuts'). There is no negative-prompt field; it goes in the prompt.

notes: Its image-to-video is natively multishot — it holds character, environment and lighting across shots inside one clip. That is why SEQUENCE and SINGLE share a graph: six framings are six shots in one take, not six clips.

ltx25-i2v.json CANNOT do first and last frame. Its two LTXVImgToVideoInplace nodes (398:349, 398:357) take the SAME image (398:350) at strengths 1 and 0.7 — base plus refine, not start plus end. TRANSITION on LTX needs the separate video_ltx2_5_flf2v template pulled down as its own graph; it has not been.
Takes one reference only, so the character sheet does not reach it.
Generates synchronized audio in the same pass — voice, effects and music.
No first/last-frame template was found, so TRANSITION has no route on this model.

wiring.server: RUNGS[4] in server.js now carries a modes map alongside variants — the mode overrides what it names and inherits the rest, so SINGLE and SEQUENCE fall through to the reference graph and TRANSITION swaps in the first-last-frame one. The page sends mode with every run; rungs without mode cells send null and the server ignores it.
